items.note: The derivation follows the proof at 741-765: the schedule rows, the net change (JV+RG)x independent of a,c, the bit and complex intersection coefficients, and the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x). The statement says 'three invocations' where the paper has three stages of v^2 invocations each. It also never gives h=100, N, m or the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection maps.

The plan states D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}. It derives them by the stored = frame(logical) invariant and by the commutation of a common frame with a pointwise gate, exactly as at 804-825.

These items are stated correctly: nested nondegenerate labels, the only decrease at center 3->4 losing h, L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L, orthonormal residual bases, and L/N=100/539 and 101/539. The route (telescoping at gates plus the loss count) is the paper's. But the actual label assignment (A,B,P,Q and the gate-label table eq:motif-labels, 899-988) and the residual table (1021-1043) are missing, so the comparability of labels is asserted rather than derived.

The plan covers the projections P_U at gates and sinks, the sources -P_{U_a}, and the frames Phi_M. It gives rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N rank-one exceptions 2P_{U_a}, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b, and the endpoint identity I_m. All of this matches 1156-1171.

The plan states that each edge's phase-frame change is a product of kernels aI+bX_v (or inverses), one per orthonormal residual vector, and that the network makes s_c calls. It omits the definition C_U=H^{(x)m} diag(i^{q_U}) H^{(x)m}, the formula s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c and the endpoint C^{(x)m} after diagonal corrections. The weight-additivity proof (1231-1315) is absent.

The steps give L<N/2, then the deficit N-2L_b>0, then eta_b,eta_c>20*2^-50 and log m<20, then m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-eta), then s_b/W_b<m^tau with tau=1-2^-50, matching 1331-1343. The exact eta values are not written, and the complex ratio s_c/W_c<m^sigma appears only implicitly in S2.2.3.7 and S5.1.1.1.
Both lemmas are stated with their O(V) bounds. S2.1.2 carries the b^{O(1)} offset-preparation condition through its quote. No derivation is given.

Both parts follow the proofs at 1375-1447. The elimination (topmost row, rightmost pivot) gives A=E_1 Pi E_2. The shear proof covers the choice of prime, the triangular updates in descending order, and the three-step pivot update that uses one interchange per one of Pi.

The steps follow 1491-1588. The plan has the k=0 base, the cyclic row split into W streams and the Phi_{A_e} edges. It gives the shear H<-H+D on every row, the interchange D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D, s calls of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with the a<=1 and a>1 cases, and the parking cost on fixed tapes.

The steps match 1649-1734: the rho high digits as rows, R=q^{2rho}>=W^k, padding to R'<2R, base-m pieces costing O(V) sum a_j m^{j tau}, and binary padding to [q^e]. The unequal-width variant is covered later in S4.2.5.

The steps cover C=HSH=aI+bX and its identities, the edge kernels over a residual basis, conjugation by P_M, inverse children via (C^{-1})^{(x)f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, s_c children on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D. All match 1835-1931.

The steps follow 2013-2200: the eight conditional additions with the parity-flip output, one cyclic shift per line, the guard interval and the bad set B, delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, repair by radix sort because T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes B, the top position by a two-bit XOR, and the stated costs.

The steps give s calls per node, an overhead of O(V((eK)^tau+1)) from the packed row additions, q_0 row chunks, the role split u=Wg+w, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the internal geometric sum, the leaf bound and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}). All match 2286-2445.

The steps state H_0 on D<=d chunks with one final truncation in O(V d^{lambda'}) time and error below sqrt2 2^{-p}. They also give the guard-width argument: E=64(W+m+1)^3, A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E using s rather than s/W, the bound 128mB^2 d^{nu+3}<=C_0 d^{C_1}, and Delta=o(p).

The steps cover character cancellation without division and F^+F^-=I/t, decimation in frequency into bit-reversed order, the reversed procedure, rounds as a parallel H plus a monomial, the layout L, the cost terms dK, pK^{tau-1} and l d^{lambda'}, and the error sqrt2 l 2^{-p}. All match the paper.

The steps follow the proof: B_0=2^{4p}, four products by the established multiplier, the separation |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, the carry ranges in packing and extraction, reduction modulo y^r+1, and the cost O(rp log(rp)).
The steps cover the retained LB order with P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the convolution rule with the scale M, error M(3delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p} and cost O(Tp[...+log(rp)]), all as in the paper.

The steps cover N=CTD with diagonal summand u_j, the cited Gaussian identity and ||N-I||<2^{-alpha^2 theta}, the Neumann inverse, A=S' and B_0=D'J'C with normalization 2^{-2alpha^2}, the ordered selection, and the unexecuted sorts. The tensor form has error dp^2 and line and axis-exposure costs. All match the paper.

The steps cover chirp periodicity, the coefficient abar_j a_{j-k} abar_k=exp(2pi i sum s_i j_i k_i/t_i), F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+ giving RF^+R=F^+, commutation with pointwise products, (u*v)/S^2, and conjugation. This is the proof at 3938-3988.

The steps give all fixed exponents and the size choices. They cover the prime-interval estimate with eta=1/(4d), disjoint intervals, T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the trial-division search, no wraparound, and c_j<2^{3b}, all as in the paper.

The steps cover the isomorphism x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, the triangular formula b_i, updates in order i=d..1, padded rotations as bijections, prefix-controlled shifts, and O(d^2) axis moves costing O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)). All match 4216-4290.
The steps cover a well-defined diagonal isomorphism with zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j and M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T. The twist error below 4h_p appears in S5.2.2.
The steps give the source transform (A, chirp, B_0, 2^gamma) with exact counterpart RF_s and the six algorithm steps from 4506-4534. They explain the two occurrences of S as undoing (u*v)/S^2.

The error chain follows the paper: E_ring<5TL, convolution error <6TL, chirp <8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, norms .26^2<.5, E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L, and a final error <448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2. Rounding is exact and the carry invariants hold.

The steps cover V=Tp, the table rows, the margins g_1..g_7 with min g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, setup and repair as o(V), log factors absorbed by p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff, matching 4815-4992. S6.3's 'g_1,g_5,g_6>1/8' is weaker than the paper's g_1,g_6>1/2 but true.
No step mentions the n log n conjecture, the eventual lower bound, or the liminf argument.

errors.says: Three invocations of a fixed schedule of linear gates exchange the two banks X,Y up to sign and restore every scratch wire.
errors.paper: There are three stages; at each stage there are v^2 separate invocations, each with its own auxiliary wires (I=3v^2). The forward/inverse/forward pattern runs stage by stage, not as three invocations.

chain: The tree reaches the main bound by the paper's route. The fixed bank-exchange network leads through frames, nested labels, the rank budget s<Wm and the power-width and arbitrary-width interchange to O(Vu^tau). The complex network, packed row additions and the layer recurrence give O(Vd^{lambda'}). Synthetic transforms and convolution, no-sort resampling with the chirp and the cancellation of R, the assembled algorithm, exact recovery and the margin table complete it. It thins out in two places: the explicit label assignment and residual table behind the budget Wm-2N+2L are asserted, not built, and the binary phase interface (definition of C_U, s_c formula, endpoint C^{(x)m}) is used without its construction.

steps.note: The fixed linear network on triples with restored scratch wires and the exchange (x,y)->(-y,x) are stated and derived. The constants h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never written: N appears only as 'data wires per bank' and m as 'dimension of the label space'.
A common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}, and each edge pays only for a change of frame.

The plan has nondegenerate labels from triple indicator vectors in a label space of dimension m, comparable labels on every edge, and only the central 3->4 edges decreasing, each by h (P(x)F(x)Q). The ambient space F^{(x)3} is not named, and the label table is omitted.
It gives rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U and the N rank-one source exceptions 2P_{U_a}, as at 1158-1165.
The plan derives sum |Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, then s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
It states L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, so the deficit N-2L_b>0 gives s_b<W_b m.
The endpoint difference P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m on X_a and I_m on every other role gives the shear H<-H+D on every role, scratch rows included.
It gives A=E_1 Pi E_2, exactly a interchanges plus O(V) per rank-a shear, and s recursive calls per node.
It gives children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), tau=1-2^-50 from eta>20*2^-50 and log m<20, and hence F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the central saving step by step in the paper's order. The bank-exchange network leads through frames, nested labels, rank equal to dimension change with N source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L/N<1/2 so s<Wm, the endpoint shear I_m, s recursive calls through the triangular factorization, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^-50. Its only gaps are the network's numerical constants (h, N, m) and the explicit label tables.
